label: accepted

evidence.V1: Silhouette render reads instantly as a bearded single-bit axe (flared crescent blade, poll stub, collar, ribbed grip, ball pommel); front and three-quarter equally clear; top view is only a pommel disc plus a tapering blade strip, which is expected for a weapon and still reads as a head-on-haft.
evidence.V2: Big forms (wide blade, haft) carry the read, medium forms (gold collar, top cap, lower band, pommel, poll) break the haft into clear zones, small detail (ink/teal wrap ridges, blade edge bevel band) is kept to the grip and edge; no uniform noise.
evidence.V3: Oversized flared blade on a short, chunky haft with a thick collar and ball pommel gives a confident stylised hatchet; A15 Y error 0.0, collar and head offsets 0.0 and both seats report seated with no gap, so no correctness cap.
evidence.V4: Chamfers are consistent across collar rims, cap, band and poll, and the blade has a continuous edge bevel that catches a light highlight along the cutting edge and spine in both studio and flat close-ups; no razor or blobby edges.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (collar, edge, grip; studio and flat) show smooth shading with no pinches, z-fighting or stray faceting; the 232 cross-shell overlaps are the neck entering the collar and are hidden; the only visible line is an intended crease where the neck flare meets the blade plane.
evidence.V6: Disciplined kit palette: gold accent (collar, bands, cap, pommel), steel grey head, one hue (teal) in two values plus ink dark for the wrap rings; colourways swap only the hue and keep gold and steel fixed.
evidence.V7: 1916 tris against the weapon target of 2500 (ceiling 4000), budget_note ok; geometry spent on silhouette (blade flare, wrap ridges) rather than hidden detail.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, kit gold/ink/steel + one hue, ~kit-scale chamfers and smooth shading; next to the PASS axe anchor it looks like the same kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Tool Handle, origin at hand/grip point, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic; all A1-A18 gates pass.

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read instantly as a bearded single-bit axe (flared crescent blade, collar, ringed grip, ball pommel); top view is a thin head line with gold cap, which is acceptable for a flat-headed axe. A15 Y error 0.0, alignment offsets 0.0, both seats seated, so no correctness cap applies.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big = flared blade, medium = gold collar and long teal haft, small = top cap, lower ferrule ring, ink grip bands and pommel ball.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised proportions: oversized flaring blade on a narrow neck, chunky collar and bulbous pommel. The flat rear poll stub behind the collar is a little thin and plate-like.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers: the blade rim has a lighter bevel band that catches light along the whole crescent, and the collar, caps and ferrule rings all have soft chamfered edges.
evidence.V5: Mostly smooth, but the close-ups show minor faceting. Where the neck lofts into the blade, a darker triangular facet pinches to a point in the middle of the blade face (visible in collar_studio/flat and as a diagonal crease in the front view). The head cheek also exits the collar cylinder with a hard cut edge (232 cross-shell overlaps).
evidence.V6: Disciplined palette: steel-grey head, teal haft in two values with ink-dark grip bands, and a gold accent on the collar, rings and pommel. The crimson and shadow colourways swap only the hue and stay coherent.
evidence.V7: 1916 tris against a weapon target of 2500 and a ceiling of 4000, so it is under target.
evidence.V8: Matches the kit: one white LF_VertexColor material, kit gold, ink, steel and one hue in values, chamfer scale and smooth shading consistent with the anchor axe.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct: Tool Handle, origin at the hand/grip point, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic.

evidence.V1: Front/three-quarter/silhouette read instantly as a single-bit axe (big flared bit, capped haft, knob pommel); top view is a thin wedge plus gold cap disk, which is as expected for an axe; A15 symmetry error 0.0 about Y and no lopsided outline.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: large flared steel bit as the big shape, gold collar + two gold rings + teal haft as medium, ink-banded ribbed grip and dome pommel as small detail concentrated at the hand end.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised proportions: oversized crescent bit with pinched neck, chunky gold collar, slightly long haft; only the back poll is a plain flat slab.
evidence.V4: Consistent ~chamfer bands on the bit edge, collar rims, ring caps and poll block that catch a clean highlight in studio close-ups; no razor edges or blobby rounding.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups of collar, edge and grip show smooth even shading: no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting; collar seats on haft (penetration intentional, A16 seated), A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: Disciplined kit palette: teal haft in two values plus ink grip bands, gold accents, steel-grey bit; colourways (crimson, shadow) swap only the hue and keep gold/steel.
evidence.V7: 1,916 tris vs weapon target 2,500 (ceiling 4,000): under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, kit gold/ink/steel + one hue, bevel width and smooth shading match the Axe_05 anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Tool Handle, origin at grip, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic - correct.

artifacts: Minor shading crease where the narrow neck flares into the blade plane (collar close-up), reads as an intended edge rather than an artifact
232 cross-shell overlaps where the head neck and poll pass into the collar (intentional interpenetration, not visible in renders)
Triangular darker facet where the neck lofts into the blade, converging to a point mid-face (front view, collar close-ups)
Head cheek and tang pass through the gold collar with a hard cut edge at the exit (cross-shell overlaps 232; allowed but visible in collar close-up)
Minor: small jog where the neck's top chamfer meets the bit's upper chamfer band (edge close-up, upper-left of bit) - a profile corner, not a shading fault
top_fixes: Add one secondary detail to the large flat blade face (shallow fuller, bevelled cheek line or a pair of rivets at the neck) so the head has medium/small detail to match the grip
Thicken the neck slightly where it leaves the collar so the head joint looks less like a thin plate slid into a cylinder
Give the poll stub a little more mass or a shaped back face so the back of the head reads better at 64 px in the front view
Re-loft the neck-to-blade transition so the taper blends smoothly into the blade face instead of forming a pinched triangular facet
Give the rear poll real mass (a short bevelled hammer or poll block) instead of the thin flat plate behind the collar
Seat the head into the collar with a cleaner socket or eye shape so the cheek does not visibly slice out of the collar cylinder
Give the back poll more shape (slight taper or rounded hammer face) so it is not a plain flat slab
Smooth the neck-to-bit transition on the top edge so the chamfer band runs continuously without the small jog
Optionally reduce grip bands from six to four-five slightly wider ones for better 64 px readability
